name: time-rfc3339
algorithm: Make n instants of 1970 to 2099 (splitmix64, seed 1, with nanoseconds), then rounds times write each as RFC 3339 in UTC with its fraction (Go's RFC3339Nano) and parse the text back; the checksum adds per instant and round the parsed nanoseconds and the text's length, wrapping.

skip.c: C's std has no RFC 3339 parser (strptime is POSIX, not in the Windows CRT, and reads no fraction or offset)
skip.rust: Rust's std has no calendar or date parser (chrono and jiff are crates)
skip.zig: Zig's std has no RFC 3339 formatter or parser
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the functions are tested against Go by the lane's Go tests (status/std-time2.md)
notes: Mk: Time.Format through Arena.Fmt (the text in an arena per round, freed at its end), then time.ParseRfc3339. Go: Time.AppendFormat into one reused buffer, then time.Parse with RFC3339Nano (its RFC 3339 fast path), which copies the text into a string first.
Checksums agree between Mk and Go at both sizes on the owner's machine (std-time2 session 2, 2026-11-13).
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
